name: Artichoke Green
lede: Artichoke Green is a soft, greyed yellow-green, named for the vegetable.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines artichoke green as the yellowish-green color of the artichoke [1]. The library records the name in Maerz and Paul's dictionary, first recorded in 1905, on plate 20 B 2 [2]. It is a textile and fashion color, grey enough to feel calm and natural [2].

Its nearest standard color is [[sage]], at a distance of 5.9, and its nearest named neighbor is Vetiver Green [2]. It belongs with the muted greens such as [[moss-green]] and [[olive]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings the color appears in 3.29% of the paintings, as photographed [3]. It is more common than 82% of the named colors and peaks in the 1900s, at 2.0 times the rate expected from the museums' baselines [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 39% of cases [3]. Zacarías González Velázquez is its most devoted painter here, with 6 of 29 works [3].
